arxiv-1809-01859.title: Deep Learning-Based Decoding for Constrained Sequence Codes
arxiv-1809-01859.creator: Congzhe Cao, Duanshun Li, and Ivan Fair
arxiv-1809-01859.description: Abstract Constrained sequence codes have been widely used in modern communication and data storage systems. Sequences encoded with constrained sequence codes satisfy constraints imposed by the physical channel, hence enabling efficient and reliable transmission of coded symbols. Traditional encoding and decoding of constrained sequence codes rely on table look-up, which is prone to errors that occur during transmission.

arxiv-1904-01693.title: Multigrid Predictive Filter Flow for Unsupervised Learning on Videos
arxiv-1904-01693.creator: Shu Kong, Charless Fowlkes
arxiv-1904-01693.description: Abstract We introduce multigrid Predictive Filter Flow (mgPFF), a framework for unsupervised learning on videos. The mgPFF takes as input a pair of frames and outputs per-pixel filters to warp one frame to the other. Compared to optical flow used for warping frames, mgPFF is more powerful in modeling sub-pixel movement and dealing with corruption (e.g., motion blur).

arxiv-2110-10187.title: Sky Is Not the Limit
arxiv-2110-10187.creator: Vojtěch Havlena, Ondřej Lengál ✉, Barbora Šmahlíková
arxiv-2110-10187.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vojtěch Havlena, Ondřej Lengál ✉, Barbora Šmahlíková. We propose several heuristics for mitigating one of the main causes of combinatorial explosion in rank-based complementation of Büchi automata (BAs): unnecessarily high bounds on the ranks of states. First, we identify elevator automata , which is a large class of BAs (generalizing semi-deterministic BAs), occurring often in practice, where ranks of states are bounded according to the structure of strongly connected components.

Misleading, unreadable, or confusing visualizations spread misinformation. Furthermore, they fail to deliver their message to the viewer. arxiv-2308-16603.description: Abstract . Theorems of Khintchine, Groshev, Jarník, and Besicovitch in Diophantine approximation are fundamental results on the metric properties of Ψ \Psi -well approximable sets. These foundational results have since been generalised to the framework of weighted Diophantine approximation for systems of real linear forms (matrices).

arxiv-2410-05254.title: GLEE: A Unified Framework and Benchmark for Language-based Economic Environments
arxiv-2410-05254.creator: Eilam Shapira, Omer Madmon, Itamar Reinman, Samuel Joseph Amouyal, Roi Reichart, Moshe Tennenholtz
arxiv-2410-05254.description: Abstract . Large Language Models (LLMs) show significant potential in economic and strategic interactions, where communication via natural language is often prevalent. This raises key questions: Do LLMs behave rationally? How do they perform compared to humans? Do they tend to reach an efficient and fair outcome? What is the role of natural language in strategic interaction?

arxiv-2412-20994.title: Atomistic modeling of the structure and diffusion processes at Al(110)/Si(001) interphase boundaries obtained by vapor deposition
arxiv-2412-20994.creator: Yang Li, Yuri Mishin
arxiv-2412-20994.description: Abstract We report on molecular dynamics simulations of the atomic structure and diffusion processes at Al(110)/Si(001) interphase boundary created by simulated vapor deposition of Al(Si) alloy onto Si(001) substrate. An array of parallel misfit dislocations of both full and partial types is observed at the interface. Si atoms segregate to the misfit dislocations, with segregation to full dislocations being stronger.

pmc-11437110.title: Prediction of android ransomware with deep learning model using hybrid cryptography
pmc-11437110.creator: K. R. Kalphana, S. Aanjankumar, M. Surya, M. S. Ramadevi, K. R. Ramela, T Anitha, N. Nagaprasad, Ramaswamy Krishnaraj
pmc-11437110.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In recent times, the number of malware on Android mobile phones has been growing, and a new kind of malware is Android ransomware. This research aims to address the emerging concerns about Android ransomware in the mobile sector. Previous studies highlight that the number of new Android ransomware is increasing annually, which poses a huge threat to the privacy of mobile phone users for sensitive data. Various existing techniques are active to detect ransomware and secure the data in the mobile cloud.

pmc-13006255.title: Embracing bilingualism in healthcare education: key stakeholders’ voices
pmc-13006255.creator: Khatmah Alanazi
pmc-13006255.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionIn recent decades, higher education institutions worldwide have increasingly adopted English as the Medium of Instruction (EMI) across various disciplines, including medicine, to promote internationalisation and enhance access to global knowledge and markets. While EMI facilitates access to international medical knowledge and improves graduates’ global competitiveness, it also introduces linguistic and cognitive challenges, particularly in non-Anglophone contexts such as Saudi Arabia.

pmc-13052614.title: De-implementation of healthcare interventions post-COVID-19: evidence from the Evidence-Based Interventions (EBI) programme in England
pmc-13052614.creator: Joel Glynn, Tim Jones, Mike Bell, Jane M Blazeby, Christopher Burton, Carmel Conefrey, Jenny Donovan, Nicola Farrar, Josie Morley, Angus GK McNair, Amanda Owen-Smith, Ellen Rule, Gail Thornton, Victoria Tucker, Iestyn Williams, Leila Rooshenas, William Hollingworth
pmc-13052614.description: AbstractObjectivesWe explored the effectiveness of the Evidence-Based Interventions (EBI) programme which aimed to reduce the number of inappropriate procedures or diagnostic tests (‘interventions’) in the English National Health Service (NHS). For 12 interventions, we evaluated whether expected intervention counts fell or geographical variation was reduced across England following the publication of EBI Wave 2 guidance in November 2020.

pmc-13101033.title: An In Vitro Model of Macrophage Senescence
pmc-13101033.creator: Grasiela Torres, Utkarsh Tripathi, Ivan Salladay‐Perez, Itzetl Avila, Anthony J Covarrubias
pmc-13101033.description: We present a reproducible in vitro protocol for harvesting and culturing murine bone marrow‐derived macrophages, with the added capability of freezing bone marrow cells at –80°C for scalability and long‐term storage. To induce macrophage senescence, we developed a genotoxic stress‐based method using either 10 Gy ionizing radiation or 500 nM doxorubicin treatment.
